page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration provides 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression tests scoring in the bottom 10% to 25% of evaluated systems. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-tier results in stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 decompression, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory read bandwidth reaches up to 654.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 75.3 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though the overall Passmark memory score remains in the lower 25% tier.

Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without demanding top-tier single-threaded compute performance. It is well-suited for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. It can also handle moderate LLM inference workloads using smaller models, though performance drops on larger models. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage.
